rows.original: Try and get to know the curvy matron of the house a little better.
rows.translation: 试着进一步了解这位身材丰满的女主人。
rows.raw: "Try and get to know the curvy matron of the house a little better."

rows.original: You remember Vasko saying he was a farmboy, and Saraxeni looks about his age. What're the odds she knows him?
rows.translation: 你记得瓦斯科说过自己曾是农家子弟，而萨拉克塞尼看起来和他年纪相仿。她认识他的可能性有多大？
rows.raw: "You remember Vasko saying he was a farmboy, and Saraxeni looks about his age. What're the odds she knows him?"

rows.original: You've no more questions. Time to hunt some monsters.
rows.translation: 你没有其他问题了。该去猎杀怪物了。
rows.raw: "You've no more questions. Time to hunt some monsters."

rows.original: "They're horrible beasts, near the size of a pony," the baroness says with a visible shudder, making her ample chest quake. "Covered in spikes and scales, with noses like... like an extra arm probing around in front of them, and claws like hatchets." [pc.bg hunter barbarian |You and Eirina exchange a glance. That's a quillock alright. |Eirina gives you a glance. "Sure sounds like a quillock." ] "Have they attacked anybody?" "Yes! Me!" Sara's cheeks flush, but she pulls up the hem of her tunic to reveal a trio of fresh, pink scars on her midriff, from navel to hip. "I heard a horrible noise just before sundown and went out to investigate. I saw something tearing up one of the fields, throwing dirt up everywhere, and hit it with my staff as hard as I could. I swear, it barely felt it! The monster just whipped around and slashed me! If I was a heartbeat slower on my feet he'd have had my kidneys for dessert." She pulls her shirt back down and frowns. "I've been terrified to let my children out of the house ever since, and none of the workers are feeling any braver. I hardly blame them, but we're going to lose what's left of the harvest if this continues much longer." You ask her, "Do these quillocks only come out at night?" "No! That's the confounding part, they're active in the day — so we can't work for fear of running into them! We hear their ungodly snorting and digging around in the fields at all hours, though, I swear..." "I'd only work in the daylight hours too, if I was a little gribblie," Eirina mutters. "Gets so damn cold at night up here."
rows.translation: “那些是可怕的野兽，几乎和矮种马一样大。”女爵明显打了个寒颤，丰满的胸脯随之抖动，“浑身尖刺和鳞片，鼻子像是……像多长了一条手臂，在身体前方到处探动，爪子则像短柄斧一样。” [pc.bg hunter barbarian |你和艾瑞娜对视一眼。没错，那就是刺甲兽。 |艾瑞娜看了你一眼。“听起来确实像刺甲兽。” ] “它们袭击过人吗？” “当然！袭击了我！”萨拉双颊泛红，却还是掀起上衣下摆，露出腰腹上三道从肚脐延伸到髋部的新鲜粉色伤痕。“日落前不久，我听见一阵可怕的动静，就出去查看。我看见某种东西正在毁坏一片田地，把泥土扬得到处都是，于是用法杖使出全力打了它。我发誓，它几乎毫无感觉！那怪物转身就给了我一爪！当时我的动作只要再慢一个心跳，它就会拿我的肾脏当甜点。” 她把衣摆放下，皱起眉头。“从那以后，我一直不敢让孩子们离开房子，工人们也没有谁更勇敢。我并不怪他们，但要是再持续下去，剩下的收成也会全部毁掉。” 你问她：“这些刺甲兽只在夜间出没吗？” “不是！这正是令人困惑的地方。它们白天也会活动——所以大家根本不敢下田，生怕遇到它们！不过我们日夜都能听见它们那邪门的哼叫和刨土声，我发誓……” “如果我是只小怪物，也只会在白天干活。”艾瑞娜低声说道，“这上面晚上冷得要命。”
rows.raw: ' "They're horrible beasts, near the size of a pony," the baroness says with a visible shudder, making her ample chest quake. "Covered in spikes and scales, with noses like... like an extra arm probing around in front of them, and claws like hatchets." [pc.bg hunter barbarian |You and Eirina exchange a glance. That's a quillock alright. |Eirina gives you a glance. "Sure sounds like a quillock." ] "Have they attacked anybody?" "Yes! Me!" Sara's cheeks flush, but she pulls up the hem of her tunic to reveal a trio of fresh, pink scars on her midriff, from navel to hip. "I heard a horrible noise just before sundown and went out to investigate. I saw something tearing up one of the fields, throwing dirt up everywhere, and hit it with my staff as hard as I could. I swear, it barely felt it! The monster just whipped around and slashed me! If I was a heartbeat slower on my feet he'd have had my kidneys for dessert." She pulls her shirt back down and frowns. "I've been terrified to let my children out of the house ever since, and none of the workers are feeling any braver. I hardly blame them, but we're going to lose what's left of the harvest if this continues much longer." You ask her, "Do these quillocks only come out at night?" "No! That's the confounding part, they're active in the day — so we can't work for fear of running into them! We hear their ungodly snorting and digging around in the fields at all hours, though, I swear..." "I'd only work in the daylight hours too, if I was a little gribblie," Eirina mutters. "Gets so damn cold at night up here." '

rows.original:
You point back down the hill to the estate's old stone wall. "Did the monsters do that?"
    
    Sara makes an embarrassed noise, and rubs at her elbow. "Ah, no. That was... during the Lion Witch's War. Our estate was raided several times by the barbarians, and, well, we never had the money to see everything properly repaired. Especially after my lord husband died."
    
    [pc.dcb
        |"Ah."
        |You wince. "Sorry."
        |"Oh no! I'm so sorry."
    ]
    
    "Mmm. A lot of the outer buildings were burned, and our villagers went closer to the city. Those that weren't captured by marauders. The crown's helped some, but things have been hard out here ever since. We barely make enough from our produce to keep up the house. But you don't need to hear about our problems, I'm sorry!"
    
    Eirina puts up a reassuring hand. "It's alright. It's good to hear what troubles the realm's facing, even of a more mundane nature."
rows.translation:
你指向山坡下庄园那道古老的石墙。“那是怪物干的吗？”
    
    萨拉尴尬地哼了一声，揉着自己的手肘。“啊，不是。那是……雄狮女巫战争期间留下的。我们的庄园曾多次遭到蛮族袭击，而且，我们一直没有足够的钱把所有地方妥善修复。尤其是在我的丈夫去世以后。”
    
    [pc.dcb
        |“啊。”
        |你皱起脸。“抱歉。”
        |“噢，不！真的很抱歉。”
    ]
    
    “嗯。许多外围建筑都被烧毁了，村民们也搬去了离城市更近的地方——那些没有被掠夺者抓走的人。王室提供过一些帮助，但从那以后，这里的日子一直很艰难。农产品的收入勉强只够维持宅邸。不过你不必听我们诉苦，对不起！”
    
    艾瑞娜安慰地抬起一只手。“没关系。了解王国正面临哪些困境是件好事，即便只是这种较为寻常的困境。”

rows.original:
"Oh, winterberries, mostly," she answers softly, coiling a lock of cyan hair around a claw. "We're only of the only estates in the principality far enough north that they'll grow. You've already missed winemaking season, though, but there's some late bloomers still on the bushes. Right now the fields are mostly onions, turnips, and peppers — and my poor red peppers seem to be what those awful monsters are after!"
    
    Sara sighs sadly. "The whole crop is just about ruined."
rows.translation:
“主要是冬莓。”她轻声回答，用一根爪子卷着一缕青色头发，“我们是公国里少数几个位置足够靠北、能种活冬莓的庄园之一。不过你已经错过酿酒季了，灌木上倒还有些晚熟的果实。目前田里主要种着洋葱、芜菁和辣椒——而我那些可怜的红辣椒，似乎正是那些可恶怪物的目标！”
    
    萨拉伤心地叹了口气。“整片作物几乎全毁了。”

rows.original:
"Oh, little Vasko, yes. I remember him." Sara points back the way you came, down the road. "His family lives maybe an hour's walk back south from here. Just commonfolk, working the land. It's remarkable their son rose so high. Why, when I was younger, no more than my daughter's age, I'd see him and his friends playing in the road. I'd throw winterberries at them sometimes; he pulled my pigtails until I cried once!" She laughs, and shakes her head. "I heard his father whipped his rear red for laying hands on a noble girl; he never bothered me again."
    
    "Does he ever come back up this way?"
    
    Sara nods. "A few times a year, to visit his family. Their baron is always so proud when he does — that's the only reason I hear about it. He preens that a chancellor of the court has come to visit, as if Vasko's made the trip to see him! Arrogant pr— partridge." She glances away, biting her lip. 
    
    [vasko.around
        |Eirina smirks. "I hope he's not still pulling your pigtails."
        
        "Haha, no, I haven't talked to him in years. The last time I saw him, he seemed so... angry, about everything. I was afraid he'd snap if I said one wrong word. I just let him look around the fields like he'd wanted, and left it at that." She sighs. "A shame. With that position of his, if he could mend that chip on his shoulder he could marry into a highborn house. He's handsome enough for it."
    ]
rows.translation:
“哦，小瓦斯科，是的，我记得他。”萨拉指向你们来时的方向，也就是道路南边，“他家离这里往南大约一个小时路程。只是普通农户，以耕作为生。他们的儿子竟能爬到如此高位，实在了不起。哎呀，我小时候——也就和我女儿现在差不多大——常看见他和朋友们在路上玩。我有时会朝他们扔冬莓；有一次他一直扯我的辫子，直到把我弄哭！”她笑着摇摇头，“听说他父亲因为他对贵族女孩动手，把他的屁股抽得通红；从那以后，他再也没来招惹我。”
    
    “他还会回到这一带吗？”
    
    萨拉点点头。“每年回来几次，探望家人。每当他回来，他们的男爵总是骄傲得不得了——我也只有因此才会听说。那人炫耀宫廷大臣前来拜访，仿佛瓦斯科是专程来看他一样！傲慢的混——鹧鸪。”她移开目光，咬了咬嘴唇。 
    
    [vasko.around
        |艾瑞娜坏笑起来。“希望他现在不会再扯你的辫子了。”
        
        “哈哈，不会；我已经很多年没和他说过话了。上次见到他时，他看起来对……一切都充满怒火。我生怕说错一个字，他就会爆发。我只是让他按照自己的意思在田里四处看看，然后便没再打扰。”她叹了口气，“真可惜。凭他的地位，如果能放下心里的怨气，完全可以迎娶高门贵族。他也确实长得足够英俊。”
    ]

rows.original: "Me?" Sara says, cheeks darkening just a touch. She rests a hand over her chest, and her aurora-tipped tail flares behind her. "I'm Saraxeni en Corina, a pleasure to make your acquaintance, my [pc.mf |lord |lady ]...?" "[pc.name][kiyoko.married | Ōtomo ][kythie.isMarried | en Tychris ][etheryn.married | var Ridell ]," you say, taking the lady's hand and giving it a kiss. [kythie.isMarried |"Oh, my! You're Lady Kythie's new [pc.mf |husband |w-wife ]! I'm sorry, your highness, I didn't recognize you!" [pc.isDK |"Next time you will, I'm sure." |You give her a disarming smile. "It's quite alright." ] ] "Such a [pc.mf |gentleman |gracious lady ]!" Sara giggles. "My daughter Stelania and son Ademn are inside. By the grace of Prince Evander, we are lords over this parcel of land, and I have the honor to be a companion of Lady Tethys when the hosts of Tychris march." You let your eyes wander over the soft, motherly curves and plush thighs in front of you. "You don't strike me as a soldier, Sara." She laughs into the back of her hand. "Oh, no, no. I am a mage. Not a particularly skilled one," she adds, glancing at Eirina, "but I spent my youth studying the arcane arts, and a bit of the sword and military tactics. My father held the same role to Prince Evander's father, and his father before him... well, you understand. I only wish that talent was enough to protect my own home! But my lightning magic seems to just bounce off these creatures!" "That's what we're here for," you say reassuringly. "You've got nothing to worry about." "I feel better already," Sara says. Her toe-claws clack excitedly against the stone porch. "Perhaps you two would like to come inside and have some food and wine with us? There's some olive bread near ready to come out of the kiln..." Eirina cuts you a glance. "We'd love to, but we really should take care of the monster problem first, don't you think, [pc.name]?" "Oh!" Sara gasps. "Of course, how silly of me." "But afterwards," you say, returning Eirina's look. "Afterwards." Eirina nods.
rows.translation: “我吗？”萨拉说道，双颊微微泛红。她把一只手放在胸口，带有极光尾焰的尾巴在身后明亮起来。“我是科丽娜家的萨拉克塞尼，很高兴认识你，我的[pc.mf |大人 |女士 ]……？” “我是[pc.name][kiyoko.married |·大友 ][kythie.isMarried |·恩·提克里斯 ][etheryn.married |·瓦尔·里德尔 ]。”你说道，牵起女士的手，在手背上轻吻一下。 [kythie.isMarried |“噢，我的天！你就是凯西女士新婚的[pc.mf |丈夫 |妻、妻子 ]！抱歉，殿下，我没有认出你来！” [pc.isDK |“我相信下次你就会认出来了。” |你露出令人放松的微笑。“完全没关系。” ] ] “真是一位[pc.mf |绅士 |优雅的女士 ]！”萨拉咯咯笑道，“我的女儿斯特拉妮娅和儿子阿德姆都在屋里。承蒙埃万德王子恩典，我们是这片土地的领主；每当提克里斯大军出征时，我也有幸作为泰西斯女士的随从同行。” 你的目光在眼前那柔软而充满母性魅力的曲线与丰腴大腿上游移。“萨拉，你看起来不像士兵。” 她用手背掩着嘴笑了起来。“噢，不，不。我是一名法师，而且算不上特别出色。”她补充道，同时瞥向艾瑞娜，“不过年轻时，我学习过奥术，也学过一点剑术和军事战术。我的父亲曾为埃万德王子的父亲担任同样的职务，他的父亲在他之前也……嗯，你明白的。我只希望自己的才能足以保护家园！可我的闪电魔法似乎只会从这些生物身上弹开！” “这正是我们来到这里的原因。”你安慰道，“你不必担心。” “我已经感觉好多了。”萨拉说道。她的趾爪兴奋地敲击石质门廊。“也许你们愿意进屋，和我们一起吃些食物、喝点酒？窑炉里有些橄榄面包，很快就能出炉……” 艾瑞娜瞥了你一眼。“我们很愿意，不过还是应该先解决怪物的问题，对吧，[pc.name]？” “噢！”萨拉倒吸一口气，“当然，我真糊涂。” “不过可以等事情结束以后。”你回应艾瑞娜的目光。 “事情结束以后。”艾瑞娜点点头。

rows.original: "Feel free to help yourself to the berries," Sara says, trying not to swish her tail too hard with interest. "They may be a little too ripe for eating, but you're more than welcome to whatever you want from the gardens, young [pc.mf |man |lady ]!" You give her a nod and head down to the bushes nearest the manse, hurriedly collecting two handfuls of overripe blue-red berries. They're already so soft that several of them just turn to mush on you, but that's fine, it's their destiny anyway. "Do you have somewhere I can set up some tools?" you call back to the porch. "Preferably open to the air?" "There's an old barn out back," Sara says. "Help yourself. Only ones you might bother are the crows." You give her a nod and set off to work. All you need to do is get a fire going, create a thick paste, boil down the winterberries, and then refine them down through a couple of good strains into a thick, viscous oil that's unpleasantly cold to the touch. Mix that in with the earthy paste, and you're good to go. It won't last long, but excite the paste against a metal surface and it'll get ice cold! "Oh, honey, it smells like wet horse out here!" Sara complains as you return, pinching her nose. Eirina just laughs. "That's alchemy for you, my lady! But I think I know what [pc.name] is about. Good thinking!" "Well, I [pc.ra astrida |expect nothing less from an Astrida |can see [pc.heShe] must be quite clever, to travel with an Astrida. ]"
rows.translation: “浆果请随意采摘。”萨拉说道，努力不让兴奋的尾巴摆得太厉害，“它们可能熟过头，不太适合直接吃，不过花园里的东西随你取用，年轻的[pc.mf |先生 |女士 ]！” 你朝她点点头，走向宅邸附近的灌木丛，迅速采了满满两捧熟过头的蓝红色浆果。它们已经软到有几颗直接在你手里化成了果泥，不过没关系，反正这就是它们注定的归宿。 “有没有地方能让我摆开工具？”你朝门廊喊道，“最好是露天的？” “后面有座旧谷仓。”萨拉说道，“随便用吧。可能会被你打扰到的也只有乌鸦。” 你点头回应，随即动手。只需要生起火，制成浓稠的糊状基料，把冬莓煮烂，然后经过几次充分过滤，将其提炼成黏稠的油；这油摸起来冷得令人不适。再把它与带有泥土气息的糊料混合，便大功告成。成品维持不了多久，但只要在金属表面激活糊料，就会变得如寒冰般冰冷！ “噢，亲爱的，这里闻起来像匹湿马！”你回来时，萨拉捏着鼻子抱怨道。 艾瑞娜只是笑了起来。“炼金术就是这样，女士！不过我想我知道[pc.name]打算做什么了。好主意！” “嗯，我[pc.ra astrida |相信阿斯特丽达理应有这般本事 |看得出[pc.heShe]必然相当聪明，才有资格与阿斯特丽达同行。 ]”

rows.original:
"Ready to head out?"
    
    Eirina gives you a nod. "Always."
    
    "Don't worry, Sara, we'll be back soon," you say. "Just stay inside until we're done."
    
    The baroness gives you a demure smile and steps back towards her door. "Goddess watch over you both! You don't know what this means to us." 
    
    When the door closes behind you both, you [pc.bg hunter barbarian
        |take a deep breath and head towards the fields. "Follow me. I'll catch the beasts' trail."
        
        "Oh, well. After you, then!"
        |give Eirina a look. "So what now?"
        
        "I'll try and find a trail, I guess! Tracking's not my strongest suit, but quillocks have pretty distinctive claw-feet. Shouldn't be too hard."
    ]
    
    The tracks are easy to spot: deep, chicken-like gouges in the earth all around the baroness's fields, where the earth's been turned up and her crops have been torn to shreds.

rows.original:
You lean in and plant a kiss on Eirina's brow. "I'm going to [pc.isMage

rows.original:
You're roused from your sleep by your lover sitting up on the bed's edge, stretching all those glorious back-muscles out right in front of you. It's enough to [pc.hasRealCock
        |give you a little stiffy right then and there
        |send a tremble of warmth between your legs
    ]. "[var0
        |Morning
        |Afternoon
        |Evening
    ], beautiful," you murmur, reaching out to grab those muscles. You just end up with a handful of fat, scaly tail, wrapping around your wrist. 
    
    "Hey, [pc.name]. Did I wake you?"
    
    You shake your head. "About time I got up too."
    
    "Good. Just hold still a second, and..." Eirina lifts a hand and incants a spell. The bed under you vibrates, just for a split second, and you suddenly smell rose petals and lilac all in the air. The scent of sex vanishes under it, almost entirely washed away. And your skin starts to feel downright pristine, too. "There! A little old rune-magic, from Old Belhar. Courtesy of my predecessor's predecessor."
    
    "Handy." You clamber over to the 'mander before she can get up, putting your arms around her. She leans back into the embrace, content to let you kiss her neck and shoulders, working your way up to her lips. You taste her lips, gently parting them with your tongue. "But that's even nicer."
    
    "Mmm. Better stop, or I'll end up derelicting my duty all over the place."
    
    "That'd be terrible," you say, slipping a hand up to her breast. One good squeeze and she's stiffening, chest heaving into your hand. "There we go. Just wanted you to keep thinking of me."
    
    "Believe me. I can't really stop." Eirina squirms out of your grasp, shaking her head. "Come on, already, before I pounce on you."
    
    "That'd be terrible," you echo.
    
    She boops your nose with a warm tail-tip, and hands you your top. Alright, alright...
rows.translation:
你的爱人坐起身来到床边，就在你面前舒展那一身壮美的背部肌肉，将你从睡梦中唤醒。这景象足以[pc.hasRealCock
        |让你当场微微勃起
        |让一股温热的颤栗掠过双腿之间
    ]。“[var0
        |早上好
        |下午好
        |晚上好
    ]，美人。”你低声说道，伸手想抓住那些肌肉，最后却只握住一大把粗壮的鳞片尾巴；尾巴随即缠上你的手腕。 
    
    “嘿，[pc.name]。我把你吵醒了吗？”
    
    你摇摇头。“我也该起床了。”
    
    “很好。保持不动一下，然后……”艾瑞娜抬起手，吟唱一道法术。你身下的床铺振动了短短一瞬，空气中忽然弥漫起玫瑰花瓣和丁香的香气。性爱留下的味道被它覆盖，几乎彻底洗净，就连你的皮肤也开始感觉洁净如新。“好了！这是老贝尔哈尔传下的一点古代符文魔法，来自我前任的前任。”
    
    “真方便。”趁这位火蜥蜴还没起身，你爬到她身边，用双臂抱住她。她向后靠进你的怀抱，满足地任由你亲吻自己的脖颈和肩膀，一路吻到嘴唇。你品尝着她的双唇，用舌头轻轻将其分开。“不过这感觉更好。”
    
    “嗯。最好停下来，否则我可要把职责抛到九霄云外了。”
    
    “那可太糟糕了。”你一边说，一边把手伸到她的乳房上。只用力捏了一下，她的身体便骤然绷紧，胸膛在你手中急促起伏。“好了。只是想让你继续惦记着我。”
    
    “相信我，我根本停不下来。”艾瑞娜扭动着挣脱你的怀抱，摇了摇头。“快点起来，不然我真要扑到你身上了。”
    
    “那可太糟糕了。”你重复道。
    
    她用温暖的尾尖轻点你的鼻子，把上衣递给你。好吧，好吧……

rows.original: You continue to pet Eirina's hair, listening to the cadence of her breath slowing, slowing... until it turns into a soft snore. Lights out, little 'mander. Once you're sure she's out cold, you slip out from under her, replacing your body with your still-warm pillow. She stretches a little, wrapping her arms around it. Even her tail tries to curl around you, swishing under the covers. Gods, she is cute, though. You shake the thought and start prowling. First, the captain's chests of drawers. You pull them open one by one, quietly shifting through folded kilts, tunics, a few formal robes... not a trace of underwear amongst them, but also nothing but clothing. Not even jewelry. You slide them closed, one after another, emptyhanded. Her nightstands prove to be only a little more helpful: she's got a couple of daggers, blank parchment and inkwells, sitting dangerously close to a few bottles of scented oil. [var0 |You draw in a sharp breath as glass clinks against glass, and Eirina's ears twitch... but that's all the reaction you get. Good. Gentle a you can, you slide the drawer closed. Nothing actually useful in there. Well, there go the obvious places. She's got an arming stand and weapon rack, but they're obvious, and well-worn. Unlikely. One last place to look, then: you lower yourself to the ground, peering underneath the bed. Sure enough, there's several wooden chests and cases under there, tucked out of sight. You brush their brass claps with your fingertips, one after the other, exerting just a little pressure. Most of them give — not locked. All but one. With all the delicacy in the world, you lift the case up and pull it a little closer. It's heavy, solid as a rock and etched with runes. [pc.isMage |Runes of warding, anti-scrying, preservation. Serious business, this. But no alarm spell, at least as far as you can see. Bit of an oversight, but you suppose in the basement of the Astrida's stronghold they aren't really worried about somebody tampering with things. You'd never be able to get down here yourself if [pc.ra astrida |you weren't one of them yourself |not for one of them falling for you ]. |You have no clue what they mean, but they don't react to you manhandling them at least. That's a good start... ] You take a deep breath and gingerly try to lift the lid. Locked tight. Damn it. Well, [pc.cl thief |you've got some lockpicks for that. You slide them out of your pack and get to work, pushing tumblers up one after the other until you hear that almost-imperceptible click of success. |the good news is that the lady with the key is probably here in the room with you. You've just got to find it. A process that's really rather quick, it turns out. Eirina's sword belt's fallen to the ground just a few paces away, and she's got a bronze ring of keys hanging off the back of it. Glancing one last time at their slumbering owner, you surreptitiously slide the keys off her belt and start going through them. Sure enough, one fits. ] You pop the lock and lift the lid. All that's inside is a single book, unmarked, plainly bound. The only embellishment is a gold-thread bookmark halfway through. You crack the cover and peer inside. On the very first page is a single sentence, inked in a flowing hand: Spells Inscribed Upon the Body of Ynes, of Courlund, as Recorded by Paladin Eirina of the Most Holy Order Astrida Now this could be useful. |And you're just a little too quick in your investigations: a pair of bottles click together, loud enough that Eirina snorts. You hurriedly close the drawer and grab your [pc.armor], trying to make it look like that made the noise. "Ugh. [pc.name]? What're you doing?" "Oh, just... just getting dressed. I thought you were dead asleep." Eirina stretches. "Light sleeper. Gotta be when you travel alone.[pc.bg soldier | You were a professional once, right? Got the look about you. "Suck suck suck suck, you suck." Eirina grabs her spear from where its leaning against the wall and shoves past you, towards Ynes's desk. rows.original:
"A ring for a giant? Uh, hold on here..." Eirina laughs. "I think I know what Kythie's talking about, but I can't just let you walk off with Philandros's ring! It's a relic from the Godswar, the very symbol of our order. We keep it enshrined down in the sanctuary. Sisters pray to it for guidance every day!"
    
    You sigh. "Can't you let me borrow it for a day?"
    
    [pc.ra astrida
        |Eirina gives you a sympathetic look. "I wish I could, but even for a member of the Order that's a tall ask.
        |"Absolutely not!" Eirina crosses her arms. "I'm sorry, really, but that ring is precious to us. I can't just let somebody, even a Champion, wander off with it in the forest. Even by my standards that's irresponsible."
    ]
    
    God damn it. "Do you have any ideas, then? The poor giant's been out there for gods-know how long."
    
    "Yeah, and I'm curious as to why... what the hell would the Blackscale Prince have hidden out in the woods of Hawkstone?" Eirina rubs her chin. "I know there was a big battle near there, where the Astrida fought. Some old fort, we were trying to hold back Wraithtouched from overrunning past the River Ridell. And then there was a lot of monster hunting the mountains after the war. Still is, once or twice a year, down near the fjords. But right in the middle of the forest?" 
    
    She shrugs. "I can't give you the ring, but maybe I have something just as good. Kythie might have been wrong about a writ. Hold here a second."
    
    The Astrida claps your shoulder and jogs off towards the downstairs door. You watch her go, [eirina.fucked
        |appreciating the bounce of all that muscular ass barely hidden by her kilt
        |feeling more than a little bewildered. Prince Evander's not in the basement, is he?
    ]
    
    Ynes [ynes.pregStage 3
        |waddles
        |swoops
    ] over to you with a cup of tea. "Well, you should feel honored, having the First Spear of the Order running from you. Even a dragon couldn't manage that. What did you say?"
    
    You just give her a look, which makes the witch cackle with mirth. She hands you the cup and slips into one of the nearby chairs, [ynes.pregStage 2
        |letting you caress her baby bump
        |thumbing through one of the books left lying out
    ] while you wait.
    
    It only takes a minute or two for Eirina to return, carrying a wooden box under her arm. "Alright! Here, this might just do it for you." She slaps the box into your waiting hand. "Take a look."
    
    Sure, you'll bite. You crack it open, revealing a time-yellowed old roll of parchment, complete with a broken wax seal depicting the Tychrisian arms. "What is this?"
    
    "A writ, from Prince Philandros himself. It's been with the Order since... actually before it was technically founded. We actually have several of these, and I'd like it back all the same, but I don't necessarily mind letting this walk out the door. It's not unique in the world."
    
    Ynes arches an eyebrow. "It certainly is precious, though, if that's what I think it is."
    
    "Yeah, so, this was like a... like a letter of introduction from the prince. Tychris was spared the worst of the fighting, since it was Nareva's stronghold, but Philandros wanted to take to the fight to the Wraiths. So he sent out chosen men to go and recruit the best soldiers, spellcasters, and scoundrels from all over the empire and bring them to Tychris. This letter gave the bearer the right to speak and bargain with his authority."
    
    "And before you ask," Ynes says, "it doesn't mean anything anymore. Don't go trying to get royal privileges with that, for goodness' sake. It's obviously centuries out of date."
    
    Eirina smirks. "Yeah, but so's your giant. She'd recognize the signature, the seal, all of it."
    
    You take the box and stow it. "We'll see [pc.isDK
        |if she falls for it
        |what she thinks
    ]."
    
    "Good luck!" Ynes says, heading back to her desk. "And don't forget to drop that in the returns bin when you're done."
    
    "Ha, yeah, I guess that's one way to do it. So, anything else you need?"
rows.translation:
“给一个巨人弄戒指？呃，先打住……”艾瑞娜笑道。“我想我知道凯西在说什么，可我不能就这么让你把菲兰德罗斯的戒指带走！那是诸神之战留下的圣物，是我们教团最根本的象征。我们把它供奉在下面的圣所里。姐妹们每天都向它祈祷，求取指引！”
    
    你叹了口气。“你就不能让我借一天吗？”
    
    [pc.ra astrida
        |艾瑞娜同情地看了你一眼。“我也希望我能，但就算是教团成员，这个请求也太过了。
        |“绝对不行！”艾瑞娜抱起双臂。“我很抱歉，真的，但那枚戒指对我们来说太珍贵了。我不能让任何人，哪怕是冠军，带着它跑进森林里到处乱晃。就算按我的标准，那也是不负责任。”
    ]
    
    真该死。“那你有什么主意吗？那可怜的巨人不知道在那儿待了多久了。”
    
    “是啊，而且我也好奇是为什么……黑鳞王子究竟把什么东西藏在了鹰棘镇的林子里？”艾瑞娜搓着下巴。“我知道那附近打过一场大战，阿斯特里达参战的那场。有座旧堡垒，我们当时想拦住亡魂侵染者，不让他们越过里德尔河。”她又说：“战后那些年，山里猎杀魔物的活儿很多。现在也还有，一年一两次，就在峡湾附近。可偏偏在森林正中央？” 
    
    她耸耸肩。“戒指我不能给你，但也许我有一样同样好用的东西。关于通行文书，凯西也许说错了。在这儿等一下。”
    
    这位阿斯特里达拍了拍你的肩膀，朝楼下的门小跑过去。你看着她离开，[eirina.fucked
        |欣赏那被她的短裙勉强遮住的肌肉臀部一颠一颠
        |感到相当困惑。埃万德王子不会就在地下室里吧？
    ]
    
    伊内斯[ynes.pregStage 3
        |摇摇摆摆地
        |飘一样地
    ]端着一杯茶走向你。“嗯，你该感到荣幸，教团的首席长矛竟为你跑前跑后。连一头龙都做不到这一点。你刚才说了什么？”
    
    你只是看了她一眼，惹得这女巫咯咯直笑。她把杯子递给你，滑进旁边的一张椅子里，[ynes.pregStage 2
        |任你抚摸她的孕肚
        |翻着随手摊在那儿的书
    ]，而你等着。
    
    只过了一两分钟，艾瑞娜就回来了，腋下夹着一个木盒。“好了！来，这个也许正合你用。”她把盒子拍进你等着的手里。“看看吧。”
    
    行，你就看看。你把它撬开，里面是一卷被岁月熏黄了的旧羊皮纸，还带着一枚破碎的蜡封，上面刻着提克里斯王室的纹章。“这是什么？”
    
    “一份通行文书，菲兰德罗斯王子亲笔的。它一直由教团保管，从……实际上从教团正式成立之前就在了。这种东西我们其实有好几份，我一样希望它回来，但也不一定介意让它出门一趟。它在世上并非独一无二。”
    
    伊内斯挑起一道眉毛。“不过它确实珍贵，前提是我想的那东西没错。”
    
    “对，所以，这就像是……像是王子的一封引荐信。提克里斯因为是娜瑞瓦的据点，避开了战事最糟的部分，但菲兰德罗斯想把战火烧到亡魂身上去。于是他派出亲选的人，去从帝国各地招募最好的士兵、施法者和亡命之徒，把他们带到提克里斯来。这封信赋予持有者以他的权威发言和谈条件的权利。”
    
    “而且省得你问，”伊内斯说，“它现在已经没有任何效力了。看在老天的份上，别拿它去讨要什么王室特权。它显然已经过时几百年了。”
    
    艾瑞娜勾起嘴角。“是啊，可你的巨人也是过时的。她会认得那个签名、那枚印章，全部都会认得。”
    
    你接过盒子收好。“那就看看[pc.isDK
        |她会不会上钩
        |她怎么想
    ]。”
    
    “祝你好运！”伊内斯说着走回她的书桌。“还有，用完了别忘了把它扔进归还箱里。”
    
    “哈，是啊，我猜这也算一种办法。那么，你还需要别的什么吗？”

It's certainly a little odd to see one of Sorra's chosen in Nareva's seat of power, and the strangeness doesn't end there, either; for starters, she's fully clothed, and quite modestly at that. A soft, woolen sweater and long skirt show off considerably less skin than the garb of any harpy you've seen, and rather than the bright and fiery colors of the harpies out west, her plumage is a gentle brown. Noticing your presence, she [dayNight |looks up at you through a pair of thick, horn-rimmed glasses, her golden, half-lidded eyes conveying a sense of palpable drowsiness |looks up from the tome she had been studying intently, craning her neck at a steep angle ] as she greets you. "[pc.swornGod nareva |Ah! You must be [pc.name]. I was wondering if I might run into you." Without waiting for a response, the stout harpy rises from her chair and extends a clawed hand, which you take. As she gives a polite handshake, the librarian gives you a warm grin, before releasing your hand. You're sorry, but how does she know you? You can't recall ever meeting this woman before. Seeing your confusion, she awkwardly stammers for a few seconds, before composing herself. Clearing her throat, she takes a step back. "A-ah, my apologies! We haven't met in person before, but, well... just about everyone in this cathedral knows of you, [pc.name]. There hasn't been a time in living memory when someone was outright inducted into the Order Astrida, rather than born into it; such news spreads quickly." You suppose that would make sense; given the unusual circumstances, you can hardly be surprised that word got around. Nodding softly, you gesture for her to continue. "A-anyways, allow me to introduce myself. I am Lystra, temporary head of the cathedral's archives. It's my pleasure to finally meet you, [pc.name]." [pc.isDK |Yeah, whatever. It's certainly a little odd to see one of Sorra's chosen in Nareva's seat of power, and the strangeness doesn't end there, either; for starters, she's fully clothed, and quite modestly at that. A soft, woolen sweater and long skirt show off considerably less skin than the garb of any harpy you've seen, and rather than the bright and fiery colors of the harpies out west, her plumage is a gentle brown. Noticing your presence, she [dayNight |looks up at you through a pair of thick, horn-rimmed glasses, her golden, half-lidded eyes conveying a sense of palpable drowsiness |looks up from the tome she had been studying intently, craning her neck at a steep angle ] as she greets you. "[pc.swornGod nareva |Ah! You must be [pc.name]. I was wondering if I might run into you." Without waiting for a response, the stout harpy rises from her chair and extends a clawed hand, which you take. As she gives a polite handshake, the librarian gives you a warm grin, before releasing your hand. You're sorry, but how does she know you? You can't recall ever meeting this woman before. Seeing your confusion, she awkwardly stammers for a few seconds, before composing herself. Clearing her throat, she takes a step back. "A-ah, my apologies! We haven't met in person before, but, well... just about everyone in this cathedral knows of you, [pc.name]. There hasn't been a time in living memory when someone was outright inducted into the Order Astrida, rather than born into it; such news spreads quickly." You suppose that would make sense; given the unusual circumstances, you can hardly be surprised that word got around. Nodding softly, you gesture for her to continue. "A-anyways, allow me to introduce myself. I am Lystra, temporary head of the cathedral's archives. It's my pleasure to finally meet you, [pc.name]." [pc.isDK |Yeah, whatever. You suppose you had to get around to meeting the other people who work here eventually |The pleasure is mutual; getting to know the temple's staff is always a delight ]. rows.original:
As you make your way to Lystra's desk, her eyes light up. Rising from her chair, she meets you as you approach, [lystra.fucked
        |throwing her arms around you in a warm hug
        |extending a hand to shake yours
    ] while you stand confused. What's all this about?
    
    Lystra steps back, excitement gleaming in her golden eyes. "Why, to congratulate you, of course! Word spreads quickly around here, [pc.name]; given the unique nature of your induction into the Order Astrida, it only seemed natural that I should offer you some personal congratulations! I was hoping you'd arrive sometime soon, and here you are!"
    
    As much as you're caught off-guard, you recover quickly. Thanking Lystra, she nods her head, and steps back. Returning to her seat, Lystra shuffles a few papers, before returning her gaze to you politely.
    
    "Now then, dear, was there anything you had needed from me?"

rows.translation: 你花了一点时间观察那位身形像鹰、面容像女人的图书管理员，然后在她对面的位置坐了下来。首先吸引你注意的，当然是莱斯特拉的不同她看起来和你们见过的任何女妖都不一样。 [dayNight |她戴着一副大框眼镜，镜片厚得是你见过的最厚的了。透过那些镜片，两只金色的大眼睛闪烁着光芒，但由于她夜行性的生活习惯，她的双眼总是半闭着，微微眯着。 |她闲暇时翻阅着一本小册子，显然，莱斯特拉更像是个夜猫子——与白天那个昏昏欲睡、话少得可怜的图书管理员截然不同，此刻的她更像是一位热心的学者。她甚至没有借助蜡烛阅读，那厚厚的眼镜使得她金色的眼睛显得更加大了。 ]她的成熟程度也远高于普通的鹰身女妖——看起来就像一位四十岁左右的人类女性，按照鹰身女妖的标准来说，她确实属于年纪较大的一类。不过，除此之外，你很快就会注意到，莱斯特拉的颜色和羽毛也显得非常独特。与那些通常被阳轻型晒成古铜色的鹰身女妖们相比，她的皮肤苍白而柔软，这显然说明她并不像大多数同类那样经常待在户外。此外，她的“头发”也有些与众不同：棕褐色的羽毛覆盖着她的头部，而那些特殊的绒毛使她的“头发”看起来像是一个松散的发髻。在你见过的所有鹰身女妖中，她与众不同——她的肩膀和脖子上覆盖着一层柔软的羽毛，还有一条短而宽的鸟尾。她的翅膀和腿部也同样长满了羽毛，这些羽毛又宽又蓬松，触感十分柔软，而她手部和足部上那些凶恶的爪子，则与这些羽毛形成了鲜明的对比。尽管动作敏捷，但莱斯特拉的手部法却轻柔而细腻，翻动书页时动作娴熟而从容。 然而，第二个同样会吸引你注意的特征，便是她的身材。 莱斯特拉身材粗壮结实，身高大约为五英尺八英寸——这显然比大多数当地的蝾螈要短得多。看来，莱斯特拉的生长过程似乎与其他蝾螈有所不同。出局而不是向上，这个假设因为她那丰满的身材而显得更加可信。两个巨大的 [lystra.isMom |乳白色的 |悬挂的；摇摆的 ] 她的毛衣将胸部衬托得格外饱满，每一个乳晕都足以容纳莱斯特拉的整个头部，甚至还有剩余。乍一看，这个露出的胸部轮廓似乎显得极为挑逗，但莱斯特拉却只觉得这不过是多了一个口袋而已；她完全没有意识到，将自己的卷轴夹在胸前，其实会带来多么引人注目的效果。 [lystra.isMom |考虑到它们的体积如此庞大，阿尔巴总是喜欢依偎在这些东西旁边也就不足为奇了……说起来，你女儿压在它们上面的重量似乎让莱斯特拉再次开始渗液了。在那件羊毛衫的正面，可以看到两处散发着淡淡甜味的潮湿痕迹，不过莱斯特拉似乎还没有注意到这一情况。 |说起来，她的体形确实没有那些女妖般丰满，但丰满的胸部在女妖群体中确实算是比较少见的现象。不禁让人好奇，她究竟是怎么做到的飞行身上挂着那些东西 ]在下面部分，情况也差不多。莱斯特拉那朴素的装束并没有过多地展示她的身材，但 [lystra.fucked |你知道下面到底是什么吧 |她那柔美的曲线使得即使她穿着普通的衣服，也足以激发人们的想象力。 ]. [lystra.pregStage 0 2 |她那柔软、圆润的…… |她那圆润、仿佛孕育着生命的身体…… ] [silly |箱子；储物箱 |中部区域 ] 从她的裙子上可以清楚地看到这一点，而那些典型的、像鹰头女妖一样宽大的臀部也丝毫没有被忽略。 [lystra.fucked |当然，鉴于你与莱斯特拉共度的那些经历，你肯定非常清楚她的穿着打扮是怎样的。确实隐藏起来吧。你肯定知道她的臀部有多么丰满诱人——厚厚的脂肪层与柔软的绒毛交织在一起，巧妙地掩盖了那些用于助跑起飞的强健腿部肌肉，从而使莱斯特拉拥有了一对堪称“完美”的大腿“靠垫”。[lystra.isMom | 毫不奇怪，生完孩子后，她的大腿变得更加丰满结实了——每一条大腿都比你的头还要粗，其柔软的脂肪组织足以让你的手陷了进去，而她那变宽的臀部更是让大腿的体积显得更加突出。 | ] 此外，与她的大腿一样，莱斯特拉紧致轻型滑的阴部也覆盖着一层柔软的绒毛——那是一丛蓬松的小绒毛。 | ] 尽管身材魁梧，但莱斯特拉的实际灵活性却出人意料。她行动敏捷，常常能在几乎无声无息的情况下突然移动，就像一只真正的猫头鹰一样——她在飞行时发出的唯一声响，也只是轻微的重击在着陆后，她的行走方式也几乎看不出来有什么不同；她的动作非常轻柔。咔嗒咔嗒声她移动时总会挥动着自己的利爪，但她的潜行能力实在无人能及——她总能不知不觉地接近目标。没人知道她是怎么做到的，但生活总有些神秘之处吧……对于在图书馆工作的人来说，这种能力无疑是非常宝贵的。总的来说，用来形容莱斯特拉的最恰当词语，恐怕就是“充满母性关怀”。 [lystra.isMom |而且不仅仅是字面意义上的那样； |即便不考虑她的外貌， ] 在大教堂里，她就像一位善良而充满关怀的存在，乐于帮助学者们和朝圣者们。 [lystra.isMom |当然，她怀里还抱着那个可爱的小宝宝。你的宝宝。[lystra.numKids 1 2 | | 最年长的 ] 女儿阿尔巴 [dayNight |她依偎在母亲的胸前，正沉沉地睡着呢。 |从莱斯特拉的腿上探出头来，暂时停止了她的写作练习。 ]由于鹰头鹫的成长速度如此之快，她现在已经有了人类幼儿般的体型，而且也同样有着强烈的求知欲。这个充满好奇心的小猫头鹰每当妈妈给她读书时，都会迫不及待地跟着学习。虽然她那连绵不断的问题可能会让人感到有些烦扰，但想到自己培养出了这样一个如此渴望学习的女儿，心中还是会感到无比自豪的。她的身臂和腿部都覆盖着柔软、绒毛般的羽毛，这些羽毛与她母亲的羽毛十分相似，只不过她的羽毛是柔和的灰色，而莱斯特拉的羽毛则是棕色的。虽然她的翅膀还没有发育到可以飞行的程度，但她无疑继承了莱斯特拉那种轻巧敏捷的体质——毫无疑问，她很快就会用自己的出现把大教堂里的访客们吓一跳的。 [dayNight |你注视着她熟睡的样子，观察着她呼吸时胸膛的轻轻起伏。毫无疑问，她此刻一定在梦里聆听母亲给她读过的那些书…… |当你注视着阿尔巴时，她正从莱斯特拉的膝上朝你微笑，然后又继续她之前的工作——把听到的单词记录下来。真是个学习能力很强的孩子啊…… ] | ]

rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_LIBRARY |Thinking on a topic, you decide to ask Lystra about [rand |her time working with the library. Does she enjoy it? Lystra [dayNight |gives a soft smile |smiles warmly ] as you ask, visibly thinking back to pleasant memories, before replying. "[dayNight |Hoo... yes, I do enjoy it |Ah, yes. I've always loved my time here ]. I've been enamored with the cathedral's archives ever since I was a chick. I distinctly recall one evening, when my father brought me along to retrieve a scroll he wished to peruse; I fell in love the moment I walked in. I spent much of my free time here, simply learning for the sake of learning; by the time I was fully grown, I knew this was what I wished to devote my life to." Lystra gently smiles as she reminisces, the twinkle of old memories in her golden eyes. So, how did she come to work here? She mentioned that Eirina somewhat abruptly placed her in charge recently, but what about before that? Lystra [dayNight |blinks in surprise, somewhat embarrassed |clears her throat, chuckling softly before she responds ]. "Well, I, ah... I asked. It must have been... oh, nearly twenty years ago now, when I did. I still remember it, mostly because it was so uncouth of me..." She adjusts her position in the chair, avoiding your gaze somewhat. "If I'm to continue, you must promise me not to laugh. I'm getting embarrassed just remembering this, you know." [pc.isDK |Do you have to? |Seriously? It can't be that bad. ] "I'm serious, dear." Lystra retorts, uncharacteristically stern. [pc.isDK |Fine, fine. Y |So be it; y ]ou promise. "Very well, then. As I was saying... one morning, I marched my way up to the front desk, and pleaded my case to lady Evadne, the previous Lorekeeper. She greeted me the same as she always did, and then, well... I begged to be able to work at the cathedral, to help others who pursued learning as I did... I said I'd do anything, make any vow, whatever it took. And when I looked up at Evadne... she was absolutely mortified." Lystra buries her neck in her fluffy collar for a moment, before continuing. "She said that I didn't have to beg, swear, or do anything; that she knew exactly how much I loved to learn, to help others to learn, and that she wouldn't dream of denying me that. And then, she said the worst part of all. That they were always accepting applicants, and I could have just taken a form from the desk." ...Wow. That is pretty embarrassing. Lystra mumbles something under her breath, then clears her throat and looks back at you. "All the same, that's the past, and this is now. In the nineteen or so years since, I've learned much, and I've loved every moment of helping the scholars and visitors to this place. I certainly never expected to be placed in charge of it, though– even temporarily." Sounds like she quite enjoys working here. |her duties to the library. What is it that she does here? Lystra takes a second to consider your question, before lifting a wing and gesturing at the enormous scroll-shelves around the cathedral. "[dayNight |Allll of this |What you see all around you ] is what I do here, dear. From my first day on the job, my duties have been the maintaining of the archives. While the shelves may appear disorderly and assorted at a glance, I can assure you that there is a system– one of my own invention. Wait, she sorts all the scrolls and tomes in the archives? How can she even manage that? Lystra gives a prideful smirk in response, clearly reveling in the indirect praise. "Well, I did, before Eirina placed me in charge, at least. It wasn't all my own work, either; the library's numerical cataloging system was the result of much effort between myself and Lorekeeper Evadne, Eirina's predecessor. Prior to its creation, our inventory was sorted variously by both order of acquisition, and the author responsible; a very confusing mixture." But how does she physically manage to do that? Between retrieval and return, you can't imagine she has the idle time to do much else. "[dayNight |Mm, well..." Lystra yawns, taking a moment to stretch her wings as she does so. " |Ah, well, ]I did specify that I did that prior to assuming leadership. Sleeping during the day can be helpful when the library is much slower at night; I would often spend the night returning the day's work back to its home. As I'm sure you can no doubt imagine, being able to fly is a useful skill for such endeavors." Lystra [dayNight |smiles softly, a gentle sense of self-satisfaction emanating from the drowsy harpy |visibly beams with pride, just a hint of smugness breaching her usual composed demeanor. Still a harpy at heart, one supposes ]. "That said, recently I've had to delegate much of the more mundane work out to other acolytes[lystra.isMom |. Not to mention, I've recently gotten... considerably busier." Lystra smiles softly, looking towards Alba before continuing. "B |, b ]ut as the temporary head of the library, I'm still both able and willing to assist anyone who may require it. Speaking of which, was there anything else which you needed?" |the history of the cathedral. What can she tell you about this place? Lystra pauses for a moment, reflecting. "Well, there's quite a lot which can be said about the cathedral, you know. I suppose I'll simply run you through the gamut." [dayNight |Lystra straightens her posture, clearing her throat as she blinks the drowsiness out of her eyes, before |Adjusting her position and clearing her throat, Lystra smiles warmly as ] she begins to recite a clearly well-practiced spiel. "The building you're currently standing in is the Cathedral of Nareva. Headquarters of the Order Astrida, foremost seat of power for the goddess of knowledge and secrets, and the largest publicly-accessible library on the continent. You'll not find its equal anywhere, a fact our Tychrisian sponsors take no small amount of pride in... as well as our staff." Lystra gives a small hoot of a chuckle at that, before resuming. "As for the actual history of the temple itself, it was constructed before the Godswar, having been built over the remains of an old animist temple by Belharan missionaries. In addition to serving as the training grounds for newly-created Astrida, the annex of the Order is also where the Astrida are created– by Nareva herself. Speaking of whom, she's been known to visit the library on occasion; I've had the honor of meeting her in person a few times." [pc.swornGod nareva |You suppose that would certainly make sense. Given the length of time Lystra's spent working at the library, it's hardly a surprise Nareva would have talked to her at least once |Wait, she's met Nareva? This may be the seat of her power, but it's still surprising to you that the goddess would have taken the time to chat with the temple staff ]. Lystra laughs gently for a moment, before smiling softly. "Yes, though it's been several years since she last made an appearance outside of the Order's compound. I do hope all is well, though I imagine she might be busy preparing for a Spellforging. We're about due for a new Astrida joining the fold, by my estimates." Lystra gently strokes her chin with a talon, thinking deeply.[pc.swornGod nareva | "Other than yourself, of course," she amends, quickly. | ] "Aside from that, there isn't all too much more to the actual history of the cathedral. With the fall of Estelore, Tychris became the de facto intellectual hub of Belhar's remains... if you consider Tychris to have been Belharan territory. It's apparently a sore spot for some, but borders and political squabbles were never my strong suit." Does she have any opinion on the matter? "I'm a harpy, dear. We live comparatively short lives, and mostly as brigands. Oddball I may be for preferring to educate myself, but I couldn't care less about where noblemen draw lines in sand." You see... "Anyways, was there something else you wished to speak about?" Lystra inquires, tilting her head. ] |Thinking back to when you and Lystra first met, a question remains. Did she say temporary head of the archives? What does that mean? Lystra shifts a little within her chair, before replying in a clearly-practiced tone of voice that indicates she's used to being asked that very question. "[dayNight |It means that, simply put, while such duties as assisting visitors usua-pardon me." Lystra yawns briefly, covering her mouth with a wing before resuming. "Usually |That's correct, yes. It means that, while such duties as assisting any important visitors with their inquiries, as well as upkeep of the cathedral's logistics, usually ] fall upon the Lorekeeper, Lady Eirina, I am instead tasked with such." Pardon your curiosity, but why is that? Lystra pauses, considering her answer for a moment. "...Well, truthfully, I'm not quite sure what's occurred. Eirina approached me a short while ago, and quite blithely stated that she would like me of all people to temporarily uphold her duties to the cathedral. I imagine she must have had a sound reason to do so, but as a humble worker here, I am of course not privy to such details. Regardless, such particularities are hardly pertinent. Is there anything else I might assist you with [dayNight |today |tonight ]?" ]
rows.translation: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_LIBRARY |在思考某个问题的时候，你决定向莱斯特拉询问相关情况。 [rand |她在图书馆工作的那段时光，她是否乐在其中呢？ 莱斯特拉 [dayNight |露出温柔的微笑 |温暖地微笑 ] 正如你所说，他显然在回忆一些美好的往事，然后才回答道。[dayNight |呼……没错，我确实很喜欢它。 |啊，没错。我真的很喜欢在这里度过的时光。 ]从我还是个小女孩的时候起，我就对这座大教堂的档案馆充满了浓厚的兴趣。我清楚地记得有一个晚上，父亲带着我去取一份他想要查阅的卷轴，而当我走进那里的那一刻，我就深深地爱上了那里。我把大部分空闲时间都花在了这里，只是为了学习而学习；等到我长大成人后，我意识到这才是我想要用一生去追求的事情。”莱斯特拉回忆起往事，温柔地微笑着，她金色的眼睛中闪烁着那些美好的回忆。 那么，她究竟是怎么来到这里工作的呢？她提到，最近艾瑞娜突然让她负责这项工作，但在此之前呢？ [dayNight |惊讶地眨了眨眼，显得有些尴尬 |她清了清嗓子，轻声笑了笑，然后才回答道。 ]嗯，我，啊……是我问的。那应该是在……哦，差不多二十年前了。我至今还记得，主要是因为我当时的行为实在太不得体了……”她在椅子上调整了自己的姿势，稍微避开了你的视线。“如果我继续说下去，你一定要答应我不要笑。光是回想这件事，我就已经觉得非常尴尬了，你知道的。 [pc.isDK |你呢？拥有去哪里？ |真的吗？不会那么糟糕吧。 ] 我是认真的，亲爱的。”莱斯特拉一反常态地严肃地说道。 [pc.isDK |好吧，好吧。Y |就这样吧。 ]好吧，那么。正如我之前所说……有一天早上，我直接去了前台，向之前的知识守护者埃瓦德娜女士陈述了我的情况。她像往常一样接待了我，然后，嗯……我就这样恳求道能够在大教堂工作，能够帮助那些像我一样追求学问的人……我说过，无论需要做什么，无论要立下什么誓言，我都会去做。而当我抬头看着埃瓦德娜时……她显得非常尴尬。”莱斯特拉把脖子埋进柔软的领子里片刻，然后继续说道。她说我不需要乞求、恳求，也不需要做任何其他事情；她说她非常清楚我有多热爱学习，有多热衷于帮助别人学习，因此她绝对不会拒绝我这样的愿望。然后，她说了最关键的那句话。他们一直在接收申请者，而我本可以直接从那里拿一份表格就可以了。 ……哇，真是这样啊。是真是有点尴尬。 莱斯特拉低声嘟囔了几句，然后清了清嗓子，再次看着你说道：“不过，那些都是过去的事了，现在才是当下。在过去的十九年左右时间里，我学到了很多，而且我非常享受帮助这些学者和游客们的每一刻。不过，我确实从未想过自己会负责管理这个地方——哪怕只是暂时负责而已。” 听起来她真的很喜欢在这里工作。 |她对图书馆应尽的责任……她在这里到底是做什么的呢？ 莱斯特拉思考了一会儿，然后抬起一只翅膀，指向大教堂周围那些巨大的卷轴架，说道：[dayNight |所有这些 |你周围所看到的一切 ] 亲爱的，这就是我在这里的工作内容。从第一天开始上班，我的职责就是负责管理这些档案。虽然这些书架看起来可能有些杂乱无章，但我可以向您保证，其实是这是一个我自己发明的系统。 等等，她居然能对其进行分类。所有那些档案馆里的卷轴和典籍？她怎么可能全部处理得过来呢？ 莱斯特拉得意地笑了笑，显然很享受这种间接的赞美。“嗯，至少在艾瑞娜安排我负责这些工作之前，我是做到的。这也不是我一个人的功劳；图书馆的数字编目系统其实是我和埃瓦德娜——艾瑞娜的前任——共同努力的结果。在这个系统建立之前，我们的图书目录是按照获取顺序或者作者来分类的，这样的分类方式让人感到非常混乱。但她究竟是怎么做到的呢？在物理层面上怎么可能做到呢？从取物到归还，她根本不可能有闲暇时间去做其他事情。[dayNight |嗯，好吧……”莱斯特拉打着哈欠，一边伸展着自己的翅膀。 |啊，好吧， ]我确实是在担任领导职责之前就决定这么做的。在夜间图书馆的运行速度较慢时，白天睡觉确实会很有帮助；我经常会熬夜把当天完成的工作重新归档到相应的位置。正如你们肯定可以想象的那样，拥有飞行能力对于这类工作来说确实是一项非常实用的技能。”——莱斯特拉 [dayNight |她轻轻地笑了，那慵懒的哈比脸上流露出一种淡淡的满足感。 |她明显洋溢着自豪之情，脸上甚至透露出一丝得意，这种情绪略微打破了她一贯沉着冷静的形象。不过，谁又能否认她内心其实仍是个“恶毒的女人”呢？ ]话虽如此，最近我确实不得不把很多那些繁琐的工作交给其他助手来处理。[lystra.isMom |更不用说，我最近的工作量……确实增多了不少。”莱斯特拉轻声笑了笑，目光转向阿尔巴，然后继续说道：“嗯。 |，b ]作为图书馆的临时负责人，我仍然有能力也有意愿帮助任何需要帮助的人。说到这里，还有其他什么你需要帮助的吗？ |这座大教堂的历史。她能告诉你关于这个地方的哪些事情呢？ 莱斯特拉停顿了一下，陷入了沉思。“嗯，关于这座大教堂，其实有很多人事可以讲述的。我想我就简单地把它们都告诉你吧。 [dayNight |莱斯特拉挺直了身子，清了清嗓子，眨了眨眼睛，驱散了眼中的睡意，然后…… “至于这座寺庙本身的历史，它是在神战之前建造的。贝尔哈兰的传教士们在一座古老的泛灵论寺庙的遗址上重建了它。除了作为新创建的阿斯特丽达战队的训练基地外，该组织的分部同时也是这些阿斯特丽达战队员的驻地。创建——这是由娜瑞瓦本人亲自完成的。说到她，据说她偶尔会去图书馆；我有幸几次与她当面见面。 [pc.swornGod nareva |你认为那样做确实很有道理。考虑到莱斯特拉在图书馆工作了这么长时间，娜瑞瓦至少和她谈过一次，这也并不奇怪。 |等等，她是见过娜瑞瓦？这里或许是她行使权力的中心，但这位女神竟然会花时间与寺庙的工作人员聊天，这还是让你感到十分惊讶吧。 ]莱斯特拉轻声笑了片刻，随后温柔地笑了起来。“是的，虽然她已经有好几年没有在教团的外面出现过了。我真心希望她一切都好，不过我想她可能正在忙于准备某种法术的锻造吧。据我估计，我们应该快要有一位新的阿斯特里达加入我们的行列了。”莱斯特拉用爪子轻轻抚摸着自己的下巴，陷入了沉思。[pc.swornGod nareva | 当然，除了你自己之外。”她迅速补充道。 | ] 除此之外，实际上并没有太多其他的内容了。历史大教堂所在的地区。随着埃斯特尔尔的陷落，提克里斯实际上成为了贝尔哈尔残余领土上的知识中心……当然，前提是人们认为提克里斯属于贝尔哈尔的领土范围。显然，这对某些人来说是个敏感话题，但边界划分和政治争端从来都不是我的强项。她对这件事有什么看法吗？ “亲爱的，我只是一只女妖罢了。我们的寿命本来就较短，而且大多以强盗的身份生活。虽然我喜欢自我学习，这种行为可能有些与众不同，但对于贵族们划定的那些界限，我根本毫不在意。你看…… “不管怎样，还有其他你想谈论的事情吗？”莱斯特拉歪着头问道。 ] |回想你们第一次遇见莱斯特拉的那一刻，还有一个问题一直萦绕在我心头：她当时有没有说过什么临时的档案主管？这是什么意思？ 莱斯特拉在椅子上稍微挪动了一下，然后用一种显然已经练习过很多次的口吻回答道，显然她已经习惯了被问到这个问题。[dayNight |简单来说，就是这样的职责。比如协助游客们……不好意思。”莱斯特拉打了个哈欠，迅速用翅膀捂住嘴巴，然后继续说道：“通常来说就是这些工作。 |没错，就是这样。这意味着，虽然诸如协助重要访客解答他们的问题，以及维护大教堂的日常运作这类职责通常是…… ] 这个任务反而落在了知识守护者艾瑞娜女士身上，所以我才被指派来处理这件事。” “请原谅我的好奇，但为什么会是这样呢？” 莱斯特拉停顿了一下，仔细考虑着该如何回答。“……说实话，我其实也不太清楚发生了什么。不久前艾瑞娜找到了我，她非常随意地表示她想要我在所有人当中，她选择暂时履行自己对大教堂的责任。我想她一定有充分的理由才会这样做，但作为这里的一名普通工作人员，我自然无从知晓这些细节。无论如何，这些具体情况其实并不重要。还有其他什么我可以帮您的吗？ [dayNight |今天 |今晚 ]?" ]
rows.raw: ' [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_LIBRARY |Thinking on a topic, you decide to ask Lystra about [rand |her time working with the library. Does she enjoy it? Lystra [dayNight |gives a soft smile |smiles warmly ] as you ask, visibly thinking back to pleasant memories, before replying. "[dayNight |Hoo... yes, I do enjoy it |Ah, yes. I've always loved my time here ]. I've been enamored with the cathedral's archives ever since I was a chick. I distinctly recall one evening, when my father brought me along to retrieve a scroll he wished to peruse; I fell in love the moment I walked in. I spent much of my free time here, simply learning for the sake of learning; by the time I was fully grown, I knew this was what I wished to devote my life to." Lystra gently smiles as she reminisces, the twinkle of old memories in her golden eyes. So, how did she come to work here? She mentioned that Eirina somewhat abruptly placed her in charge recently, but what about before that? Lystra [dayNight |blinks in surprise, somewhat embarrassed |clears her throat, chuckling softly before she responds ]. "Well, I, ah... I asked. It must have been... oh, nearly twenty years ago now, when I did. I still remember it, mostly because it was so uncouth of me..." She adjusts her position in the chair, avoiding your gaze somewhat. "If I'm to continue, you must promise me not to laugh. I'm getting embarrassed just remembering this, you know." [pc.isDK |Do you have to? |Seriously? It can't be that bad. ] "I'm serious, dear." Lystra retorts, uncharacteristically stern. [pc.isDK |Fine, fine. Y |So be it; y ]ou promise. "Very well, then. As I was saying... one morning, I marched my way up to the front desk, and pleaded my case to lady Evadne, the previous Lorekeeper. She greeted me the same as she always did, and then, well... I begged to be able to work at the cathedral, to help others who pursued learning as I did... I said I'd do anything, make any vow, whatever it took. And when I looked up at Evadne... she was absolutely mortified." Lystra buries her neck in her fluffy collar for a moment, before continuing. "She said that I didn't have to beg, swear, or do anything; that she knew exactly how much I loved to learn, to help others to learn, and that she wouldn't dream of denying me that. And then, she said the worst part of all. That they were always accepting applicants, and I could have just taken a form from the desk." ...Wow. That is pretty embarrassing. Lystra mumbles something under her breath, then clears her throat and looks back at you. "All the same, that's the past, and this is now. In the nineteen or so years since, I've learned much, and I've loved every moment of helping the scholars and visitors to this place. I certainly never expected to be placed in charge of it, though– even temporarily." Sounds like she quite enjoys working here. |her duties to the library. What is it that she does here? Lystra takes a second to consider your question, before lifting a wing and gesturing at the enormous scroll-shelves around the cathedral. "[dayNight |Allll of this |What you see all around you ] is what I do here, dear. From my first day on the job, my duties have been the maintaining of the archives. While the shelves may appear disorderly and assorted at a glance, I can assure you that there is a system– one of my own invention. Wait, she sorts all the scrolls and tomes in the archives? How can she even manage that? Lystra gives a prideful smirk in response, clearly reveling in the indirect praise. "Well, I did, before Eirina placed me in charge, at least. It wasn't all my own work, either; the library's numerical cataloging system was the result of much effort between myself and Lorekeeper Evadne, Eirina's predecessor. Prior to its creation, our inventory was sorted variously by both order of acquisition, and the author responsible; a very confusing mixture." But how does she physically manage to do that? Between retrieval and return, you can't imagine she has the idle time to do much else. "[dayNight |Mm, well..." Lystra yawns, taking a moment to stretch her wings as she does so. " |Ah, well, ]I did specify that I did that prior to assuming leadership. Sleeping during the day can be helpful when the library is much slower at night; I would often spend the night returning the day's work back to its home. As I'm sure you can no doubt imagine, being able to fly is a useful skill for such endeavors." Lystra [dayNight |smiles softly, a gentle sense of self-satisfaction emanating from the drowsy harpy |visibly beams with pride, just a hint of smugness breaching her usual composed demeanor. Still a harpy at heart, one supposes ]. "That said, recently I've had to delegate much of the more mundane work out to other acolytes[lystra.isMom |. Not to mention, I've recently gotten... considerably busier." Lystra smiles softly, looking towards Alba before continuing. "B |, b ]ut as the temporary head of the library, I'm still both able and willing to assist anyone who may require it. Speaking of which, was there anything else which you needed?" |the history of the cathedral. What can she tell you about this place? Lystra pauses for a moment, reflecting. "Well, there's quite a lot which can be said about the cathedral, you know. I suppose I'll simply run you through the gamut." [dayNight |Lystra straightens her posture, clearing her throat as she blinks the drowsiness out of her eyes, before |Adjusting her position and clearing her throat, Lystra smiles warmly as ] she begins to recite a clearly well-practiced spiel. "The building you're currently standing in is the Cathedral of Nareva. Headquarters of the Order Astrida, foremost seat of power for the goddess of knowledge and secrets, and the largest publicly-accessible library on the continent. You'll not find its equal anywhere, a fact our Tychrisian sponsors take no small amount of pride in... as well as our staff." Lystra gives a small hoot of a chuckle at that, before resuming. "As for the actual history of the temple itself, it was constructed before the Godswar, having been built over the remains of an old animist temple by Belharan missionaries. In addition to serving as the training grounds for newly-created Astrida, the annex of the Order is also where the Astrida are created– by Nareva herself. Speaking of whom, she's been known to visit the library on occasion; I've had the honor of meeting her in person a few times." [pc.swornGod nareva |You suppose that would certainly make sense. Given the length of time Lystra's spent working at the library, it's hardly a surprise Nareva would have talked to her at least once |Wait, she's met Nareva? This may be the seat of her power, but it's still surprising to you that the goddess would have taken the time to chat with the temple staff ]. Lystra laughs gently for a moment, before smiling softly. "Yes, though it's been several years since she last made an appearance outside of the Order's compound. I do hope all is well, though I imagine she might be busy preparing for a Spellforging. We're about due for a new Astrida joining the fold, by my estimates." Lystra gently strokes her chin with a talon, thinking deeply.[pc.swornGod nareva | "Other than yourself, of course," she amends, quickly. | ] "Aside from that, there isn't all too much more to the actual history of the cathedral. With the fall of Estelore, Tychris became the de facto intellectual hub of Belhar's remains... if you consider Tychris to have been Belharan territory. It's apparently a sore spot for some, but borders and political squabbles were never my strong suit." Does she have any opinion on the matter? "I'm a harpy, dear. We live comparatively short lives, and mostly as brigands. Oddball I may be for preferring to educate myself, but I couldn't care less about where noblemen draw lines in sand." You see... "Anyways, was there something else you wished to speak about?" Lystra inquires, tilting her head. ] |Thinking back to when you and Lystra first met, a question remains. Did she say temporary head of the archives? What does that mean? Lystra shifts a little within her chair, before replying in a clearly-practiced tone of voice that indicates she's used to being asked that very question. "[dayNight |It means that, simply put, while such duties as assisting visitors usua-pardon me." Lystra yawns briefly, covering her mouth with a wing before resuming. "Usually |That's correct, yes. It means that, while such duties as assisting any important visitors with their inquiries, as well as upkeep of the cathedral's logistics, usually ] fall upon the Lorekeeper, Lady Eirina, I am instead tasked with such." Pardon your curiosity, but why is that? Lystra pauses, considering her answer for a moment. "...Well, truthfully, I'm not quite sure what's occurred. Eirina approached me a short while ago, and quite blithely stated that she would like me of all people to temporarily uphold her duties to the cathedral. I imagine she must have had a sound reason to do so, but as a humble worker here, I am of course not privy to such details. Regardless, such particularities are hardly pertinent. Is there anything else I might assist you with [dayNight |today |tonight ]?" ] '

rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_HERSELF |Thinking on possible topics, you settle on [rand |Lystra's family. She mentioned her mother raised her; what is she like? Lystra smiles softly at your question, a kind expression as nods her head. "As a matter of fact, my mother and father have both been there to raise me. I’m well aware that’s quite uncommon for harpies; though, the way they met is certainly more of what you may expect." Oh? "You see, my mother used to be a thief, though not the sort of banditry common among the harpies of the Marches. Back when she was a young, scrawny thing, she happened upon my father’s merchant-cart one night, and swooped down to grab a bundle of food... and instead fetched a very frightened salamander with a bad habit of sleeping on his merchandise. From the way I heard it, his companions managed to wrestle her to the ground, and asked my father what to do with her." Lystra chuckles softly before she resumes. "Rather than truss her up and leave her, or exact a... carnal sort of revenge, or do something even more nefarious, he simply said to get some food from one of the packs and give it to her, then leave her be. According to her, that simple act of kindness won her heart." And then? "She followed him for days. He told his companions not to drive her off, but to let her keep following from a distance. He'd leave spare rations out for her, and she'd swipe them every night. One morning, just before the dawn, she approached my father's sleeping pack, leaned down, and said, quite bluntly, that she loved him." [pc.isDK |Good lord, you think you're going to gag |...Wow ]. "I know, right?" Lystra agrees, laughing. "The two of them were inseparable after that. She stuck with him for the remainder of his travels, and eventually moved to Tychris with him when he returned. I was born soon after, and my sister followed a year later. The three of them still run a store down in the city, and I visit often." Sounds like she had it pretty good, then. "Oh, absolutely. I'd be a fool not to see how fortunate I've been in life.[lystra.isMom | Furthermore, I know Alba here will have all three of them to rely on for support as well as you and I. I couldn't be happier with the way things have turned out." |" ] Lystra smiles warmly at you, then clears her throat gently. "So, was there anything else you wished to speak about?" |Lystra's interests. What is it that she likes to do? Lystra [dayNight |blinks confusedly a few times, as if not understanding the question |Stares at you for a few moments, confused ]. "Well... I like to read. That much should be a fairly obvious inference, given my choice of career. Aside from that, though..." Lystra scratches her chin, deep in thought. "Hmm. I suppose one could say my interests are quite narrow, actually. I mean, I quite enjoy reading to others as well; I often do so for the young Astrida, as well as the children of the other staff. [lystra.isMom |Of course, that also includes ours." Lystra adds, gently stroking Alba on the head. " | ]I quite enjoy doing that– to learn is to improve oneself, and one should always aim ever upwards. Helping the latest generation to do so is the greatest joy one can attain." [pc.dcb |So she just sits in the library and reads all day? You can't imagine doing something so boring all day. What does she even read? |What is it that she reads in particular, though? She must have a favorite subject. |Ugh... that must be, like, soooo many books. Are they, like, at least about fun stuff? ] Lystra's eyes light up at your question, visibly excited. "[pc.dcb |Oh, everything! But |Of course! I read a bit of everything, but |The most fun of all! What I read is ] mostly classical literature. In my youth however, I avidly read magical theory. I'm no mage, myself– I never had the knack for it, but it was a profoundly interesting field to me all the same." What spurred her to switch subjects? [dayNight |Lystra frowns a bit, then begins softly gesturing around the room at the enormous shelves of scrolls |Lystra chuckles dryly — an unusual note of sarcasm from her, then begins gesturing at the towering scroll-shelves throughout the library ]. "Do you see all of these scrolls, tomes, and tablets, [pc.name]? I could learn every spell emblazoned upon them, teach myself the mechanics behind each and every minute detail, and by the time I would think I had mastered them, I would be over a century past my lifespan. And this is just what we make publicly accessible. I am, unfortunately, a perfectionist with magic; so much so that it's a detriment. The skill I lacked for magic was composure; I'd panic the moment any detail went awry. That's chiefly why I gave up on it; it interests me still, but there would be no use in learning it. Knowledge you never use may as well be forgotten, for all the good it does you." Lystra lowers her wing, and her warm smile returns as she meets your gaze once more. "Of course, those are simply my own personal foibles. Reading the works of authors long gone is merely something I can derive greater personal satisfaction from, and thus, it is what I chose to pursue. At any rate: was there anything else you wished to inquire about?" |Lystra's personal life. What’s she got going on in her day-to-day? Lystra [lystra.isMom |[dayNight |gives you a quizzical look, amplified further by her drowsiness |laughs softly, amused by the directness of the question ]. Taking a moment before she begins to gesture at Alba, she meets your eyes with a bemused expression. "Well, as of recently, quite a bit is going on in my life, [pc.name]. I should think you were aware of that much already, but I know what you meant. Alba's been quite the handful lately, but I still have my duties to uphold. Once the... situation with the Order is resolved, I think I may take some personal time, let her properly have some family time with her aunt and grandparents. Aside from that however, things are mostly the same as it ever was. [silly |Letting the days go by, and whatnot |Another day, another night, more of the same ]. Not that I mind, of course. There's something to be said for consistency and routine, after all. Between Alba [lystra.numKids 1 2 |and |as well as the others, plus ] my extra duties, my hands are quite full, so my own hobbies have made their way to the sidelines given the circumstances." What about any other happenings in her life? Lystra laughs softly, meeting your gaze directly. "Well, aside from a certain someone recently becoming the apple of my eye, not much else has changed– at least in my work life." Lystra gives you a slight wink at that, before leaning back into her chair a bit. "Though, now that you mention it, I have noticed that nobody's... well, made a pass at me in a while. Gods, to think, for all those years, everyone might have been serious..." [pc.isDK |The way you see it, if they didn't have the strength of will to keep trying like you did, they didn't deserve someone like her |It's unfortunate, but you're certainly not going to complain about how things turned out; you're glad to be the one Lystra loves. ]. Lystra gives you a warm smile, her face lightening in response. "Why, thank you, [pc.name]. It means a lot to me to hear you say that. At any rate, however, we ought to save the bedroom talk for the bedroom. Was there anything else you wished to discuss?" |[dayNight |nods softly |leans back in her chair a bit ] as she listens to your question, before replying. "Mm... not all that much, to tell the truth. I am, admittedly, rather a plain woman. I'm quite busy with my duties to the library lately, and as such, my free time has been playing second fiddle to that for a while now. Not that I mind, though. I've dedicated my life towards this library, and being asked to maintain it as the head, even temporarily, is an incredible honor." rows.raw: " [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_HERSELF |Thinking on possible topics, you settle on [rand |Lystra's family. She mentioned her mother raised her; what is she like? Lystra smiles softly at your question, a kind expression as nods her head. "As a matter of fact, my mother and father have both been there to raise me. I’m well aware that’s quite uncommon for harpies; though, the way they met is certainly more of what you may expect." Oh? "You see, my mother used to be a thief, though not the sort of banditry common among the harpies of the Marches. Back when she was a young, scrawny thing, she happened upon my father’s merchant-cart one night, and swooped down to grab a bundle of food... and instead fetched a very frightened salamander with a bad habit of sleeping on his merchandise. From the way I heard it, his companions managed to wrestle her to the ground, and asked my father what to do with her." Lystra chuckles softly before she resumes. "Rather than truss her up and leave her, or exact a... carnal sort of revenge, or do something even more nefarious, he simply said to get some food from one of the packs and give it to her, then leave her be. According to her, that simple act of kindness won her heart." And then? "She followed him for days. He told his companions not to drive her off, but to let her keep following from a distance. He'd leave spare rations out for her, and she'd swipe them every night. One morning, just before the dawn, she approached my father's sleeping pack, leaned down, and said, quite bluntly, that she loved him." [pc.isDK |Good lord, you think you're going to gag |...Wow ]. "I know, right?" Lystra agrees, laughing. "The two of them were inseparable after that. She stuck with him for the remainder of his travels, and eventually moved to Tychris with him when he returned. I was born soon after, and my sister followed a year later. The three of them still run a store down in the city, and I visit often." Sounds like she had it pretty good, then. "Oh, absolutely. I'd be a fool not to see how fortunate I've been in life.[lystra.isMom | Furthermore, I know Alba here will have all three of them to rely on for support as well as you and I. I couldn't be happier with the way things have turned out." |" ] Lystra smiles warmly at you, then clears her throat gently. " | ]I quite enjoy doing that– to learn is to improve oneself, and one should always aim ever upwards. Helping the latest generation to do so is the greatest joy one can attain." Between Alba [lystra.numKids 1 2 |and |as well as the others, plus ] my extra duties, my hands are quite full, so my own hobbies have made their way to the sidelines given the circumstances." What about any other happenings in her life? Lystra laughs softly, meeting your gaze directly. "Well, aside from a certain someone recently becoming the apple of my eye, not much else has changed– at least in my work life." Lystra gives you a slight wink at that, before leaning back into her chair a bit. "Though, now that you mention it, I have noticed that nobody's... well, made a pass at me in a while. Gods, to think, for all those years, everyone might have been serious..." [pc.isDK |The way you see it, if they didn't have the strength of will to keep trying like you did, they didn't deserve someone like her |It's unfortunate, but you're certainly not going to complain about how things turned out; you're glad to be the one Lystra loves. ]. Lystra gives you a warm smile, her face lightening in response. "Why, thank you, [pc.name]. It means a lot to me to hear you say that. At any rate, however, we ought to save the bedroom talk for the bedroom. Was there anything else you wished to discuss?" |[dayNight |nods softly |leans back in her chair a bit ] as she listens to your question, before replying. "Mm... not all that much, to tell the truth. [pc.isDK |So she's content to just waste her life away in a dusty old library |She doesn't mind sacrificing her personal time like that ]? Lystra frowns a bit, tilting her head at you as she hears that. "No, I wouldn't quite say that. It's simply that I understand the circumstances must be dire for such a task to fall upon a humble acolyte like myself, and harbor no objections to the will of the Goddess. It's not like I'm missing out on all that much, anyhow– aside from [lystra.fucked |a certain someone becoming the apple of my eye recently |the occasional scholar or Astrida asking me on a date as a prank ], I don't have much going on in my life. Lystra all but squawks in distress, before composing herself. "Ahem. At any rate, this is hardly a topic to discuss publicly. What else did you wish to speak about? |...As a prank? Lystra snickers a little bit, covering her mouth with a wing. "Hoo... yes, of course. I mean, it's so patently absurd! I suspect it's some sort of hazing ritual amongst the newly-training Astrida: a test of courage, perhaps. 'Oh, you think you're brave? Why don't you go ask the old lady for a date, then?' Lystra guffaws, and you're treated to the sight of [silly |those fat fucking owl tits |her enormous chest ] bouncing and jiggling as she does. Right, nothing at all... "Hoo... at any rate, [pc.name], I should thank you for the laugh. Was there anything else you wished to speak about?" ] ] ] |You've got to ask: What's the deal with Lystra, exactly? "[dayNight |Hoo... it seems everyone asks that eventually |Well, I suppose that was to be expected ]. Yes, I'm aware my appearance is rather... unique, at least for the area. [dayNight |Lystra's half-lidded eyes have the warmth of old memories in them |Lystra smiles fondly, relishing old memories ] as she continues. The foremost divergence is actually our plumage: the structure of our feathers means that, while harpies like myself fly slower, we can do so nearly silently." You imagine that must be helpful in a library of all places. [dayNight |Very much so. I'd demonstrate, but I'm quite tired at the moment... that said, |Lystra smiles proudly, brimming over with childlike glee. "I know, isn't it? You'd think it was a blessing from Sorra herself! rows.original: [flags.LYSTRA_TLK_TYCHRIS |Opting to rack Lystra's brain a bit about Tychris, you decide to ask about her thoughts on [rand |the royal family. What’s her opinion on Prince Evander and the lot? Lystra raises an eyebrow in intrigue, a glint of curiosity in those golden eyes. "Oh? The royal family, you say? That’s certainly an odd line of questioning, [kythie.isMarried |especially from yourself |if you don’t mind my stating of such ]. Why is it that you ask?" You’re not entirely sure yourself; you suppose you’re just curious about what she thinks of the rulers of the place. "Well, I'm certainly not one for politics myself, but I suppose I can answer your question. What I think of Prince Evander is that the poor boy needs to put on a few pounds. If he took a page out of his friend Kelsaz's book, it would at least make his public image seem a little more imposing. I suspect half the populace is worried Lady Tethys may one day snap him in half by accident. From the political perspective, he is, in a historical sense, unremarkable." Well, that seems a bit blunt. Surely he isn't that bad. Lystra tilts her head quizzically at you, her eyebrows raised in confusion. "I never said being unremarkable was a bad thing, dear. Just think about it, for a moment: if every leader were some ambitious warmaster, or tore up old traditions to trailblaze a path forward, the world would be even more chaotic than it already is. The squabbling warlords of the heartlands are a fine example; such constant upheaval only puts the common man at risk. History needs the mediocre. Those who maintain the status quo are just as, if not even more important than those who change it up. Besides, he's a perfectly good person, even if his leadership seems unimpressive." Lystra returns to her usual, relaxed pose as she smiles softly. "He's the bookish sort, and regularly peruses the library. I've helped him quite a few times; once, he even made a pass at me, in jest. I suspect one of the Astrida must have dared him to as a test of courage; either way, it was quite amusing.[lystra.fucked | ...At least, I certainly hope it was in jest." Lystra adds, concern showing on her face, |" Lystra chuckles, ] before taking a moment to compose herself. "It's a shame Princess Kythie didn't inherit that nature. She comes to visit on rare occasion, but it's been quite some time since I last saw her. I do hope she's well." [var0 |She's doing much better now, though you're not sure she's going to the library any time soon. Changing the subject |...Deciding to hold your tongue ], you ask Lystra if there're any other thoughts she has about the royal family. "Hm... not particularly, no. Altogether, the lot of them are, in my opinion, perfectly suitable rulers, though it's not as if I've ever known different. They're surprisingly grounded, compared to what you may expect; the concerns of the common folk truly do seem to matter to them, and they prize merit over the circumstances of birth. You can just look at their magister, Vasko, for that. They sponsored his education, and helped forge a natural talent into incredible skill; that alone merits praise, as far as I would believe." [vasko.isDreamless |Lystra frowns, shaking her head sadly. "A shame to see the way he repaid such kindness, though. I suppose the world will always have those who bite the hand which feeds them..." | ] [kythie.isMarried |Lystra laughs for a moment, before she turns to look at you. "Though, I must ask, [pc.name]: Why are you asking me about them? They're your family now, after all." |[var1 |Lystra awkwardly shifts in her seat, turning her eyes downward as she mutters. "That said... ah, as, I'm sure you learned, angering them is... not wise. You have my condolences about... that whole affair." ] ] |the city itself. What does she think of the place? Lystra takes a moment to think, gently stroking her chin with a talon as she does so. "Hm... I suppose I may not be the best judge of that, to tell you the truth. I’ve lived in Tychris all my life; having never known different, I find it difficult to give you an honest assessment of the city. For what it’s worth, though, I quite like it here. Were it not for being born in a place with such access to education, I doubt I would be anything like the woman I am today; for that, I have Tychris to thank, as well as my parents. The city’s unique role as a center for knowledge is certainly one of its greater selling points, and the glassblowing industry is, of course, what we are historically known for. As an interesting fact, we actually produce the highest number of mages per capita in the entire Marches; it’s something of a local pride point." It seems like Lystra's fairly knowledgeable about the intellectual side of things; what about the rest? Lystra [dayNight |sharply exhales |gives a soft laugh ] by way of response, shrugging. "Well, you've got me there, [pc.name]. It's rather obvious I'm no athlete. Tychris is known for athleticism, however. The Tychathlon always draws visitors, and competitors from all over the Frost Marches are known to travel for it. Perhaps the only thing comparable would be the events held in the colosseum of Khor'Minos; though, having never seen such, I am a poor judge. Aside from the markets and the aforementioned, Tychris is a fairly simple place; this very temple is likely one of the largest attractions therein. Aside from that, there isn't all that much more to say; I'm a simple woman, and I quite enjoy Tychris, inasmuch as it is where I was born, where I grew up, and where I work." Lystra states, gently yet firmly. ] |So, what can Lystra tell you about Tychris? Lystra smiles kindly, before she tilts her head at a slight angle. "Well, that depends on what you'd like to know, dear. I'm not much for city life; I prefer to spend my days at the cathedral. That said, I know a good deal about the local history, so I suppose I could tell you about that." Lystra pauses, thinking for a moment before she continues. "Tychris, as you no doubt are aware, is a hereditary principality, which has been ruled by the En Tychris line since its founding. Originally a trade hub, Tychris quickly grew into a burgeoning city-state as the Belharan Empire facilitated a constant flow of commercial trade; even with its collapse, Tychris has remained steadfast, and, in some ways, improved." Improved? How so? You can't imagine the Godswar went particularly well for anyone. Lystra nods her head slowly in agreement. "Well, I suppose those in Kitsuhon may disagree, but you're correct that Tychris fell from grace somewhat in the immediate aftermath. The loss of the heir, and arguably the spare at the outset of the Godswar certainly caused some... difficulties, the nature of which are well-documented. But through Nareva's protection, Tychris weathered the storm, and has continued to grow into the intellectual hub it is today. Likewise, the glassblowing industry has not faced the setbacks which, say, metallurgy has, and the study of magic has only ever grown since the Godswar concluded. For all that was lost to the world when Estelore fell, the archives of Tychris remain; and they're not going anywhere." Anything else she can tell you? Lystra ponders the question for a moment, before shaking her head in a particularly odd way. "I'm afraid I'm not much of a historian, dear. Harpies like myself aren't usually the type to maintain detailed records, and for all that I've read, other topics interest me further." You see. ]
